title: Bison workspace provisioning · result
description: Response body of the webhook (responseMode: lastNode) and the return value of the sub-workflow. Also the shape persisted to client_sequencers.setup_state, minus `candidates`. Deliberately the same shape as the Aimfox result so the portal renders one component for both sequencers — the differences are `sequencer`, the id format of workspace_id, and that the tag step is called `tags` rather than `labels`. It must never contain an api_key: the gateway derives booleans and the key stays server-side (process doc, invariant 7). NOTE, pre-existing and unresolved: the LISTING response (Needs Selection's `resolution.listing` branch) does not conform to this schema and never has — it sends `client_id: null` against a `format: uuid`, `state: "workspace_list"` against an enum that does not contain it, and `steps: {}` against five required keys. It is a different message wearing the same envelope (WorkspaceSetupResult in view-contracts.ts admits it, this schema does not). Splitting it into its own contract is tracked separately; adding `routing` to steps.required in 2026-08 did not create the gap but does widen it.

state.description: configured = the whole canonical set is present. partial = some elements were missing (and were created unless dry_run). missing = the workspace resolved but nothing was wired. needs_selection = the workspace could not be resolved unambiguously and a human must choose. client_not_found = the client_id matched no client with an enabled connector — a caller error, reported out loud rather than allowed to end the run silently. Computed from key, webhooks and tags only, and campaigns stay out of it even though the workflow now creates them: a created campaign is a DRAFT with no sequence, so folding it in would let `configured` mean "ready to send" while nothing can send. OOO routing pointed at a draft fails silently — the FortumEnergia shape. Routing is excluded for the identical reason: a rule pointing at a draft is not a working rule, so folding it in would let `configured` mean "out-of-office replies are being followed up" while nothing can send.

reason.description: Present when state is needs_selection or client_not_found. Says why in one sentence, so the operator does not have to open the execution.

workspace_id.description: Numeric string — Bison ids are integers, unlike Aimfox UUIDs.

matched_by.description: Resolution order, first hit wins. `explicit` — the caller supplied the id. `stored` — client_sequencers already holds one for this client. `name` — exactly one workspace matched the client name. No fuzzy value exists on purpose: an inexact match must terminate in needs_selection (invariant 2).

personal_team.description: From GET /api/workspaces/v1.1. Kept because Bison workspace names repeat far more than Aimfox's, and personal_team / main / parent_id are what let an operator tell two same-named rows apart.

campaigns.description: The three OOO automation campaigns, created as DRAFTS (POST /api/campaigns with a name and type: reply_followup, then POST /api/campaigns/{id}/schedule). What was blocked was never the campaign — it was POST /api/campaigns/v1.1/{id}/sequence-steps, whose copy does not exist in a usable form (all three bodies on the old canvas are the same feminine-Polish text with a hardcoded {PANIEKAMILU} placeholder). That call is never made here: a manager writes the sequence and starts the campaign, and a draft with no sequence sends nothing. Each entry in `present` carries the vendor status in brackets — `OOO automation | general (draft)` — because the name alone reads identically for a campaign that is actually sending and one that never will be.

routing.description: The three OOO routing rules (client_ooo_routing), one per routing_key: male, female, general. Provisioning fills an EMPTY rule and never re-points a full one — a rule aimed at a campaign Bison has stopped or completed is reported in `missing` with the note `existing rule kept`, not repaired, because re-pointing needs the campaign fixed at the vendor first and this workflow cannot tell a campaign that broke from one a manager stopped on purpose. That case is the majority in production: on 2026-08-19, 22 of the 25 active rules across 12 of 16 Active clients pointed at a campaign that could not send. A rule is only filled from a ROUTABLE campaign — active, launching or draft. `draft` counts as routable because that is the shape a new client's triple is born in; `completed` and `stopped` do not, because filling an empty rule with a dead campaign turns an honest `routing_missing` (visible, recoverable) into episodes that resolve and get dropped at the vendor. `present` uses the same routable test rather than `active`, so re-checking a client this workflow provisioned does not flip the step from `created` back to `missing` with nothing having changed. A duplicate campaign name yields NO target and blocks that key's rule — which of two identically named campaigns is live is not a question this workflow may guess at. This step is what the last run SAW; the live truth is the OOO routing section in the client drawer and the Clients grid's OOO column, both derived on read.

candidates.description: Only present when state is needs_selection. Already filtered: every workspace whose id appears in client_sequencers, for any client and any sequencer, is excluded — offering one would invite the misassignment that put GIC's Aimfox workspace on Prac.Finansowa.

recorded.description: Whether the run persisted itself to client_sequencers.setup_state and integration_sync_runs. False means the vendor work may well have happened while the record of it did not — the caller must not treat a failed record as a failed provisioning.

record_error.description: Present only when recorded is false. The database error, so the discrepancy is diagnosable without opening the execution.

outcome.description: ok = already present, nothing done. created = was missing and has been created. missing = was missing and was NOT created (dry_run, or a step that never creates). skipped = the step could not run because an earlier one failed. failed = the vendor rejected the call.

present.description: Element identities already at the vendor. Webhooks are identified as "<events joined by +> <url>", never by name — UniTalk's is called "Reply Classification" where every other workspace says "Reply classification" (invariant 4).
